1. The frames show a rent-versus-buy comparison using an illustrative character, Nina. One side is an apartment building with a "RENT 5%" sign. The other is a house with a red roof, with figures standing beside it. The header cites FHFA home prices, BLS rents and Freddie Mac rates as the data sources. Each frame carries the caption "US only · history, not a forecast". Frame 3 states an assumption: rent starts at $1,667 a month and rises 5% a year.

2. The camera moves from a wide view of the neighborhood to a close-up of the apartment and a figure. It then pulls back to the wide scene again. Across frames 1, 4, 5 and 6, a stack of gold blocks beside the apartment grows. A gold block also appears near the apartment's upper windows in frame 5. The rent sign shrinks as the shot widens. Some apartment windows change from lit to dark. The house and its figures drift toward the right edge of the frame.

3. The animation seems to be tracking cumulative money over time. The gold stack probably represents rent paid or savings building up, and the rent rises 5% a year on the renting side. The house side is shown next to it for comparison. The frames don't show any numbers for interest, property tax, insurance or repairs, or any final total. They don't show which option comes out ahead.

4. The frames contain no explicit advice. The only guidance is in the caption and labels. The caption says this is US history and not a forecast. The labels say the scenario is illustrative and the 5% rent growth is an assumption. A viewer could take away that rent rising each year adds up, and that the result depends on the assumptions. A viewer could not conclude from these frames that buying is cheaper or that renting is.

5. The advice in 4 comes from the on-screen text, specifically the "history, not a forecast", "ILLUSTRATIVE" and "(assumption)" labels. The idea that rent compounds and adds up comes partly from my own reading of the growing gold stack, and the animation doesn't state it. The animation never tells the viewer to buy or to rent. Any such conclusion would be my own.
